pages.title: Bottom & Top Quarks
pages.text: The third and final generation. The bottom is heavy; the top is as massive as a gold atom and decays before it can form a hadron. They are rarer than anything else in the Standard Model, and holding them feels like holding a pair of collapsing weights.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The second generation was not enough; colliding strange and charm quarks with pentaquarks in the Hyperion Synchrotron pushed collision energy high enough. Quark-gluon plasma caught the heaviest quarks before they could decay.
